newsitem.title: USA: CME live, feeder cattle end up on short covering.
newsitem.headline: CME live, feeder cattle end up on short covering.

text.p: Short covering developed late in both CME live and feeder cattle futures and prices ended higher in light dealings, traders said.
Live cattle closed 0.075 to 0.200 cent per lb higher with June up the least at 65.225 cents. Feeder cattle finished up 0.400 to unchanged with August up 0.350 at 77.650 cents.

June live cattle held technical support near the 40-day average and moved up on light short covering. Buying found little scale-up resistance and the sharp gains in pork complex futures sparked spillover demand in cattle that offset a weak tone to cash markets, traders said.

Concern that cash cattle prices have gone into a seasonal decline weighed on futures early while the discount futures hold to cash prices curbed losses. Packers were able to buy fed cattle $1 per cwt lower this week at $67 and expectations are for cattle to trade at $66 next week. Prices especially look weak after the Memorial Day holiday on Monday which itself reduces the kill rate next week, they said.

Longs and shorts both rolled out of June positions which limited the late recovery. Cargill Investor Services bought August late after selling early. LIT division of First Options also bought August, pit sources said.

In live cattle options, commission houses bought June 64 and 65 puts and 66 calls while commercials sold June 66 puts early. Commercials did October 66/72 and August 64/66 risk reversals late, pit sources added.

Feeder cattle futures also recovered late on short covering which lifted futures into buy stops. Strength in other livestock pits and lack of follow-through selling from the early decline prompted the covering, traders said.
Feeders will likely follow live cattle as any weakness or strength there would indicate demand for replacement feeders, they said.

Some traders said cash feeder cattle markets were topping, especially with the seasonal trend for fed cattle markets seen lower in the next few weeks. Technically the market is also looking toppy, they added.
The latest CME feeder cattle index rose $0.04 to $76.37 per cwt.

Lind-Waldock bought August while Refco sold and bought October, traders said. Rosenthal Collins bought August early and Cargill Investor Services spread long December live cattle/short August feeders, pit sources said.
